critical_code_review_comments: server.py /preview (line ~323): max_rows/max_cols are int query params without bounds. A malicious/large request (max_rows=1000000, max_cols=1000000) would allocate a huge grid pre-truncation because rows are appended before the length check on the outer break. The inner slicing '[:max_cols]' bounds columns per row, and outer break bounds rows, so effective memory is O(max_rows * max_cols) — still unbounded. Add Field(ge=1, le=200) equivalent validation.

/preview auto-detection: 'first row with 3+ non-empty cells' is a heuristic — for sheets with 1–2 columns of real data this will fall back to (1,1) even if the true header is on row 5. Consider also honoring an explicit query param when the frontend already knows the answer.

'__EMPTY__' magic string is used as sentinel in both the model and _build_map_rows. Consider a module-level constant (STATUS_EMPTY_SENTINEL = '__EMPTY__') to avoid drift between endpoints, and document it in the API spec so frontend/backend stay in sync.
MapUpdate.status_visible_values is List[str] with no validation — a client could accidentally send duplicates or whitespace-only entries; consider normalizing (strip, dedupe) on write.
map_data (line ~624) response now returns both 'status_column' and includes 'map' (which also has status_column) — mild duplication carried over from iteration 4.
server.py has grown to ~730 lines. Continued growth reinforces prior recommendation to split into routers before adding more features.

The /preview endpoint doesn't cache the workbook; every call to /preview -> /data -> /data re-downloads the .xlsx from Graph. For large files this is expensive; consider a short-lived (e.g. 60s) in-memory cache keyed by (user_id, file_id) with etag/lastModifiedDateTime invalidation.
